one_liner: Magento/Adobe Commerce has broad REST and GraphQL web APIs, but each merchant hosts its own instance, so credentials are per-customer; the supplied pages do not document the auth details or an MCP server.
auth_notes: The supplied pages do not cover Web API authentication. Prior knowledge (not verified here) is that integrations use OAuth 1.0a signed requests, admin and customer tokens are exchanged for a username and password, and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service uses Adobe IMS OAuth2. The fetched pages only show that Commerce Services use license-owner-generated API keys.
access_notes: The pages do not confirm that Magento Open Source is free. They show that Commerce Services API keys come only from the license owner, and that the SaaS and PaaS sandboxes need a Technology Partner Program account. Keeping the earlier value at low confidence: a developer can likely run their own Open Source store, but each merchant holds its own credentials.
blocker_notes: Every merchant runs its own instance, so a toolkit needs a per-customer base URL and credentials. Sandbox environments for Commerce are gated behind the partner program.

evidence.quote: The Commerce Web APIs allow you to integrate third-party software and build headless applications for Adobe Commerce. The Web API documentation is divided into three guides: REST, GraphQL, and Getting Started.
Only the Commerce license owner can generate these API keys.
All developers are eligible to use the **production** Marketplace EQP API.
